title: Peacemaking
tomorrow: who gets invited when they can't pay you back?

segments.voice: Yesterday, truth: said in a voice that wants someone to grow. Your line was truth in love. Today, when two other people stop talking.
screen: `TRUTH IN LOVE.` → `WHEN TWO PEOPLE STOP TALKING.`

segments.voice: Two friends, one fight, and a group chat that has gone completely silent. Each of them is now texting you separately. The easy moves are picking a side, or muting both and waiting it out. Jesus has a blessing for the one caught in the middle: “Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” Makers. Not keepers, not avoiders.
screen: `ONE FIGHT, A SILENT CHAT.` → `PICK A SIDE, OR MUTE BOTH?` → `BLESSED ARE THE PEACEMAKERS.`

segments.voice: Peacekeeping keeps things quiet. Peacemaking builds something that wasn't there, and it costs more. Jesus even puts it ahead of worship: “if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother.” First. The offering can wait; the person can't. Paul is realistic about it: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” If it be possible: some peace can't happen yet, and nobody has to stay near harm to make it. As much as lieth in you: your side of it, not theirs. And Ephesians names the deepest version, Christ breaking down “the middle wall of partition between us,” making two peoples one. For Christians, a wall coming down between people sits close to the heart of the faith. In a friendship, the work is smaller. Talk to each person alone, and don't carry gossip back. Say what's true about both. Ask each one what they need. Then, if they're ready, get them into one room.
screen: `MAKERS, NOT KEEPERS.` · `LEAVE THY GIFT; FIRST BE RECONCILED.` · `AS MUCH AS LIETH IN YOU.` · `THE MIDDLE WALL BROKEN DOWN.` · then, large: `MAKE PEACE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one strained relationship, yours or one you stand between. Write the first message of a peace: no blame, one true and kind thing, and a question. Send it if it's safe and right; if not, keep it, and hold that person in mind for the sit.
Peacemaking. Not keeping things quiet, but building peace between people, starting from your own side.
Pocket this one: make peace, as much as lieth in you, and no further than is safe. Day 1734, done.

screen: `DAY 1734 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 53 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHO GETS INVITED WHEN THEY CAN'T PAY YOU BACK?`

howItsDone: In some churches the congregation shares a sign of peace, a handshake or embrace, during worship; Christians also practice reconciliation through confession, mediation and the steps of Matthew 18.

chat.meaning: Jesus blesses peacemakers, not peacekeepers. Paul says as much as lieth in you: your part, alone with each, then an invitation back together.
